# Lifecycle and Durability Checklist: Single Multi-Repository Service

**Purpose**: Formally review whether requirements fully define registry durability and isolated multi-project lifecycle behavior before implementation
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are lifecycle requirements defined for startup, dynamic reload, restart, dispatch, retry, reconciliation, cancellation, terminal cleanup, removal, and partial failure wherever each path applies? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-012–FR-016, Spec §FR-020–FR-021]
- [ ] CHK002 Are durable registry requirements complete for creation, restoration, corruption, unreadable storage, interrupted writes, and unsupported versions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004–FR-006, Spec §FR-015, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for both fresh empty startup and returning to the empty state after the final project is removed or disabled? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the persisted Project Registration fields and explicit exclusions sufficient to prevent workflow policy or credentials from entering the registry? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-005, Spec §FR-018]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the canonical workflow path identity rule unambiguous for relative paths, symlinks, path aliases, duplicate IDs, and duplicate registrations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "active issue work" defined consistently to include active, retrying, quota-waiting, and blocked work when removal safety is evaluated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK007 Is an "actionable" unavailable or removal reason constrained enough to be safe, bounded, project-scoped, and useful to an operator? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the boundary between service-level aggregate resources and project-scoped workflow, tracker, retry, checkpoint, and workspace state explicit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-016–FR-017, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are the retained-registration recovery requirements consistent across the clarification, acceptance scenario, edge cases, FR-021, and SC-004/SC-006? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §US4, Spec §FR-021, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Are add and remove semantics consistent between dashboard and CLI requirements, including validation, idempotency, refusal, and reflected state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008–FR-014, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK011 Are local-only persistence requirements consistent with the legacy positional-workflow migration requirement and the prohibition on divergent singleton service modes? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-019]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 Can empty startup, dynamic activation, restart restoration, idempotent mutation, and interface agreement each be objectively measured from the specified outcomes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-002, Spec §SC-004–SC-005, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the requirement to operate at least 10 projects precise about preserving project attribution and workspace isolation under that load? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK014 Are failure-isolation outcomes measurable for invalid workflows, workspace conflicts, registry corruption, and project reload failures without relying on implementation details? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Are concurrent duplicate and conflicting mutations covered with requirements for serialization, idempotent results, and no partially persisted state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014–FR-015, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are recovery requirements complete when a workflow becomes invalid both during startup restoration and during ongoing operation, then later becomes valid? [Recovery, Spec §FR-016, Spec §FR-021, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a project runtime failing while other projects have active work and shared status surfaces remain available? [Exception Flow, Spec §US1, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK018 Are removal requirements complete for idle, busy, already-absent, last-project, and persistence-failure cases without deleting repositories, workflows, workspaces, or history? [Coverage, Spec §US3, Spec §FR-012–FR-015, Spec §FR-020]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK019 Are workspace collision and repository-boundary requirements explicit for every registration and restored activation path? [Safety, Spec §FR-010, Spec §SC-003, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 Are secret-safety requirements stated for persistence, dashboard, CLI, machine-readable status, and logs, including malformed input and raw exceptions? [Security, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-018, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK021 Are observability requirements complete for project attribution on issue rows, failures, runtime transitions, and aggregate status projections? [Observability, Spec §FR-017]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK022 Is the trusted-local-operator assumption bounded so it does not weaken CSRF, credential, workspace, or repository safety requirements? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK023 Are repository-owned workflow policy and the service registry clearly separated so there is one source of truth for each kind of configuration? [Dependency, Spec §FR-003–FR-005, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the browser path-selection assumption explicit about requiring a host-resolvable absolute workflow path without copying or uploading workflow content? [Assumption, Spec §FR-008, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
